description: Verify that the original module file no longer exists or has been renamed, and that two new module files exist with the expected names.
Ensure that all public functions/classes from the original module are now defined in either module_a or module_b, with no duplicates.
command: python -c "import module_a, module_b; names_a = set(dir(module_a)); names_b = set(dir(module_b)); assert not (names_a & names_b) - {'__name__', '__doc__', '__package__', '__loader__', '__spec__', '__file__', '__cached__', '__builtins__'}"

description: Run the existing test suite to confirm that behavior has not changed after the split.
Verify that no circular imports exist between the two new modules.
command: python -c "import module_a; import module_b; import sys; assert 'module_a' not in sys.modules.get('module_b', {}).get('__dict__', {}) and 'module_b' not in sys.modules.get('module_a', {}).get('__dict__', {})"

description: Confirm that the refactor.md file documents the split, including the names of the two new modules and a brief rationale.
command: grep -q 'module_a' refactor.md && grep -q 'module_b' refactor.md && grep -qi 'split' refactor.md
